A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ParallaxRAG. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison, including equations, tables, and rendered figures. Relocated material was matched; the prompt and three case-study pages are identical.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval, question-answering, ablation, transfer, and attention-head analysis results on WebQSP and CWQ.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds BioASQ evaluation and additional generator/context configurations.

M1.justification: Symmetric multi-head representations, PSR, forward/reverse propagation, query-aware gating, shared MLP scoring, and weighted listwise training are retained. Renaming DDE to DE and specifying propagation more explicitly do not establish a changed procedure. The one-shot prompt mentioned in v2 already appears in v1 Figure 6.

E1.justification: V2 adds biomedical BioASQ Task B, covering Yes/No, Factoid, and List questions beyond WebQSP/CWQ. This substantially extends domain and task coverage. Answer-in-KG subsets remain represented through hallucination-score evaluation despite removal of their separate QA table.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 adds a standalone-LLM comparison suite on BioASQ: Deepseek-R1-8B, GPT4-Turbo, and GPT-4o. These comparisons are absent from v1. The established WebQSP/CWQ retrieval and KGQA comparator methods remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen3-30B evaluations with 100/200/500 triples, GPT-4o with 200 triples, and CWQ-trained retrieval with Qwen3-Plus on BioASQ using task-specific metrics. Reported retrieval-timing hardware changes from RTX 4090 to RTX 6000 Ada. These additions and reported setting changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds biomedical transfer without retriever retraining and tests sensitivity to retrieved-context size, extending robustness analysis along two distinct axes. Existing component ablations, head interventions, alternative-encoder analyses, PSR sensitivity plots, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the DDD estimate's confidence interval and p-value, bootstrap/permutation procedures, and sample-grouped five-fold linear probing. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, or new benchmark uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New BioASQ and generator/context results substantially expand reported outcomes. Table 1's CWQ 2-hop/at-least-3-hop answer recall changes from 0.928/0.753 to 0.935/0.771; Table 4's single-vector CWQ Macro-F1/Hit changes from 46.86/55.73 to 44.82/52.63. Transfer Macro-F1 changes from 44.14 to 45.28. Most subset QA entries disappear, while many hallucination scores are retained elsewhere. SubgraphRAG's main QA scores also change, but v2 omits its generator label, preventing a secure same-setting comparison.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.2 explicitly defines the previously abstract message-passing operator through normalized neighbor aggregation and a layer weight matrix. This is a limited formal specification. The PSR derivation, weighted objective, head-metric definitions, and DDD formulation otherwise remain mathematically equivalent; no new proof is added.

C1.justification: V1's abstract claims competitive performance under a unified BGE-M3/Llama3.1-8B setup; v2 claims state-of-the-art retrieval and QA plus biomedical generalization. V2 also elevates head specialization into an explanation of a structural mismatch in existing KG-RAG, broadening the central scientific framing.

C2.justification: V2 adds limitations concerning KG/encoder quality and static graphs, and interprets BioASQ list performance as favoring precision over recall. The shallow-query failure discussed in Section 5 already existed in Appendix D. V1's explicit shortest-path versus answer-recall trade-off discussion is removed.

D1.justification: V1 promises code release upon acceptance; v2 supplies a repository access link. Conversely, v2 removes the dataset/preprocessing subsection, split-count table, subgraph provenance, and two-RTX-4090 server specification. Most training hyperparameters and the prompt remain. These are substantial documentation/access changes, without evidence that the omitted data-processing settings themselves changed.

R1.justification: Citation coverage narrows through removal of background and dataset references, including Brown et al. (2020), Huang et al. (2025), Yih et al. (2016), and Talmor and Berant (2018). The related-work taxonomy and positioning relative to MRAG and established KG-RAG approaches remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed. A domain-generalization section is inserted, the conclusion is replaced by limitations/future work, and the dataset appendix subsection is removed. Author information and DDE/DE terminology also change.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn and reformatted. The main QA table gains generator rows and hallucination columns; BioASQ receives a new table, while the separate subset-QA and dataset-statistics tables disappear. The ablation table is compressed and displays are relocated. Figures 3–9 retain their underlying visual content.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful domain-transfer and generator/context evidence, clearer limitations, and code access information. However, it removes reproducibility details and most subset QA results, leaves the BioASQ data/KG setup underspecified, and replaces the explicitly labeled SubgraphRAG/Llama comparison with an unspecified-generator row. Retained hallucination-improvement figures also no longer match the displayed baseline differences. These gains and reporting losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
